author: reek
body: Agent management in the dev console. DevAgent is a local AI that runs on the device -- DevAgent loads a GGUF model, runs inference via the NeuralNet/Tensor stack, and provides a chat interface for code assistance. For hard problems DevAgent escalates to an upstream server with a larger model.

author: reek
body: Three acquisition paths: bundled on the .img, loaded from USB, or downloaded from network. First boot walks through setup.

author: reek
body: The registry could be written to and read back by name, and that was the whole of it: nothing could ask what was IN it. The dev console's Agent Manager answered "Registry: 0 agents" from a literal for exactly as long, which is a sentence that looks like a reading and is not one.

author: reek
body: The menu keys, mapped to the configs they promise. None for a key that names no role, so a caller can tell an unknown key from a role that happens to leave the agent where it was.

author: reek
body: The title is a constant because the dispatcher matches on it to tell the role keys from the agent keys. Two spellings of the same string, one in the menu and one in the comparison, is a silent dead menu the first time either is reworded.

author: reek
body: One line per agent, and the role is on it. Without the role a swap is invisible: the console would report the same text before and after, which is indistinguishable from a swap that did nothing.

author: reek
body: `format-gpu-status` above reads a field that `gpu-bridge-init` sets to True unconditionally, so it reports READY on a machine with no host serving compute at all. It is kept because callers hold a bridge and want its declared state; it is not an answer to "is the bridge working".

author: reek
body: This is. It rings the doorbell with a 2x2 matmul whose answer is four distinct non-zero numbers, none of them an operand: [[1,2],[3,4]] times [[5,6],[7,8]] is [[19,22],[43,50]]. A host that is not there answers None, a host that echoes its input answers the operands, and a host that replies with zeros fails the comparison. Only real arithmetic passes.

author: reek
body: The cost is four values in and four out on a fixed command buffer that is mapped from boot, so the probe allocates one small tensor pair per call and no part of it grows with anything.
